merges.why: polydimethylsiloxane rubber; the survivor is the canonical silicone node
merges.loserDescription: Polydimethylsiloxane. The base polymer is made by ring-opening polymerisation of octamethylcyclotetrasiloxane or by equilibration of a silanol-terminated PDMS; fillers (silica, silicone oil) tune the hardness and the tear strength.

loserFacts.label: Cure
loserFacts.value: peroxide (e.g. dicumyl peroxide) or addition-cure platinum

loserFacts.label: Shore hardness
loserFacts.value: Shore A 40-70 for a contact pad

merges.why: Vinyl chloride monomer, same substance, same level. 70-petrochem publishes the canonical material node (with the -13.4 C boiling point, the angiosarcoma hazard and the 1983 capacity figure) and 40-chassis has a third copy at c64.case.other-polymers.vinyl-chloride. Mine is the only one carrying the oxychlorination and chlor-alkali chain down to halite, so move that subtree under chem.pvc.vcm before deleting this id.
merges.loserDescription: Made by the oxychlorination of ethylene with oxygen and chlorine over a fluidised bed of copper(II) chloride at 180-220 C, or by the chlorination of acetylene. Vinyl chloride monomer is acutely toxic and carcinogenic, and its manufacture was one of the worst occupational hazards in the chemical industry until the 1970s-80s control campaigns.

loserFacts.label: Route
loserFacts.value: C2H4 + Cl2 + 1/2 O2 -> C2H3Cl + HCl, CuCl2 catalyst, 200 C

merges.why: The RF modulator's ferrite-loaded coil exists in both fragments. metal.ferrite.modulator is the canonical published node and the rule is to link to it rather than keep a path-local copy; the 50-power version carries the schematic detail worth moving across first - a tapped coil or miniature two-winding transformer on a 2-3 mm former, 1-2 uH class at 60 MHz, 0.15-0.25 mm enamelled copper, 3-8 turns, and the note that the PAL UHF version scales the inductance down about tenfold. I have pointed the coil's material edge at metal.ferrite.nizn rather than at metal.ferrite, which keeps the branch to six nodes instead of twenty-nine.
merges.loserDescription: A very small ferrite- or powdered-iron-cored coil wound on a 2-3 mm former with a tap, or a miniature two-winding transformer. The tapped winding gives both the feedback tap and an output tap, and the whole assembly sits within a few millimetres of the board's ground plane to keep the stray capacitance stable.

loserFacts.label: Inductance
loserFacts.value: ~1-2 uH class for a 60 MHz tank, loaded by the divider

loserFacts.label: Core
loserFacts.value: ferrite or powdered iron, 2-4 mm diameter

merges.survivorName: The wave-solder pot and its dross
merges.why: Solder pot and wave former. Same machine. metal.solder.pot carries the dross and the oxide film; if the board fragment wants the machine as a component it should reference metal.solder.pot rather than own a second one.
merges.loserDescription: A stainless or cast-iron pot holding tens to hundreds of kg of molten solder at roughly 250 deg C. Inside, a pump or a tilted paddle throws solder up against a forming dam, which spills over as a smooth standing wave. The pot is lined or plated because molten tin dissolves iron: a bare iron pot would be eaten away in weeks, taking the wave geometry with it. That single material decision is what makes a wave machine a five-year purchase rather than a consumable.

loserFacts.label: Pot metal
loserFacts.value: cast iron with solder-resistant plating, or solid stainless

loserFacts.label: Wave height
loserFacts.value: a few millimetres above the pot lip, set by pump rate

merges.why: 'Electronic-grade hydrofluoric acid' is a purified grade of the same molecule, not a different substance. If the grade is worth keeping it belongs as a named grade under metal.hydrofluoric-acid. Same argument for chem.fab-chemicals.hydrochloric-acid -> metal.hydrochloric-acid.
merges.loserDescription: The silicon etchant. HF dissolves silicon dioxide, and it does so fast, cleanly and without leaving a residue - which is why it is the single most important wet chemical in a silicon fab and also the one that produces the most fatalities. Anhydrous HF is made from fluorspar (CaF2) with sulphuric acid at 200-250 C, and the aqueous grades are made from that. Buffered oxide etch dilutes hydrofluoric acid to 0.5-5% and buffers it with ammonium acetate or acetic acid to hold the pH at 4-6, and the buffer is not cosmetic: it stabilises the etch rate by controlling the HF2- concentration and stops the etch accelerating as the acid is consumed.

merges.why: the fab's ultrapure water is the cross-cutting utility, and facility.water.ultrapure is the node the rest of the tree already points at (CHECKLIST 1a). Keep this fragment's four facts (resistivity, TOC, particle count, temperature) by moving them across; do not leave two nodes with the same name.
merges.loserDescription: The most-consumed chemical in a fab by volume, and the hardest. Deionised, reverse-osmosed, ultrafiltered, UV-irradiated and finally ozonised to a resistivity of 18.2 MOhm-cm at 25 C, with total organic carbon below 5 parts per billion and dissolved silica below 1 part per billion. The resistivity figure is a saturation: it says the water is at the limit of what a deioniser can do, and it was the number on the certificate that every batch of chemicals was diluted from.

loserFacts.label: Consumption
loserFacts.value: thousands of cubic metres a day for a mid-size fab

merges.why: same monomer. Three copies survive now (facility.steam.styrene, peripheral.tv.cabinet.abs.styrene, c64.case.abs-resin.styrene); the general one should survive. If the 40-chassis or 90-peripherals node turns out to be the richer one, keep that instead and re-point the divinylbenzene sibling edge.
merges.loserDescription: Vinylbenzene, made by catalytic dehydrogenation of ethylbenzene or recovered from a cracker. A 1980s ABS plant bought it at 99.5% or better into stainless bulk tanks, inhibited against polymerisation in transit.

merges.survivorName: Cleaning the flux residue off the board
merges.why: CROSS-REFERENCE, NOT A MERGE - please do not apply this one as a merge. The same step (washing rosin flux residue off a soldered board) is written twice: as an assembly operation in this fragment and as a waste-stream problem in 60-metals.json. Both readings earn their place, so this wants one node with two aspects, or at minimum a cross-link. Both are left in place and mb.assembly.cleaning's note says so.
merges.loserDescription: Rosin flux leaves a sticky, slightly conductive, hygroscopic and mildly acidic film. The board is washed - historically in an isopropanol or detergent wash, sometimes with a little ultrasonics - and then dried. The film matters rather than the shine: rosin residue is hygroscopic and mildly acidic, so in humid climates it slowly corrodes the board and lowers surface insulation between adjacent pads.

loserFacts.label: Consequence if skipped
loserFacts.value: surface leakage and, over years, corrosion

merges.survivorName: Graft copolymerisation: growing SAN on the rubber
merges.why: same process, same chemistry; chem.abs.grafting already carries the graft-copolymerisation route and the rubber phase
merges.loserDescription: The dominant ABS route since the 1960s and still the one that makes the resin in the C64. Butadiene is polymerised in water to a polybutadiene latex; styrene and acrylonitrile are graft-polymerised onto that latex; the graft latex is coagulated, dewatered, dried and compounded with separately made bulk-SAN resin.

loserFacts.label: Initiation
loserFacts.value: potassium or sodium persulfate, or an organic persulfate

loserFacts.label: Residual monomer removal
loserFacts.value: steam stripping in a vacuum plate column

merges.why: the SAN matrix component is already a node there; mine is a second copy of it
merges.loserDescription: Most ABS is a blend: grafted rubber plus a separately polymerised SAN. The SAN is the continuous, glossy, rigid phase; the grafted rubber is the dispersed, toughening phase. The SAN is usually made by bulk or emulsion polymerisation in a separate plant and shipped to the ABS compounding line as pellets or as latex.

loserFacts.label: Typical AN content in the SAN
Share of SAN in the finished ABS

merges.why: the 1980s ABS additive package is already written out there
merges.loserDescription: ABS pellets as delivered are a straw-coloured, unpigmented polymer. The beige-brown of the C64 case is added downstream at the compounder as a colour masterbatch, together with stabilisers, a release agent and, in some grades, a flame retardant. A 1982 C64 case is almost certainly pigmented at the compound line, not at the moulder. The lightening and browning that a case shows over forty years is the butadiene rubber phase oxidising at the surface, so both the UV stabiliser loading and the pigment loading affect how fast it happens.

merges.why: twin-screw compounding and pelletising, already published there with the same equipment children
merges.loserDescription: Natural ABS pellets are let down with the colour masterbatch and additives on a co-rotating twin-screw extruder, degassed, filtered through a screen pack, and pelletised - chopped strands or underwater cut. This is a 1980s standard plastic-compounding line.

loserFacts.label: Throughput (merchant line)
loserFacts.value: a few hundred kg/h to 1-2 t/h

merges.why: drying ABS before moulding is already a node under chem.abs
merges.loserDescription: ABS is hygroscopic: even a little absorbed water hydrolyses the nitrile groups at melt temperature, causing splay streaks and reduced molecular weight. Pellets are dried before use - typically 2-4 hours at 80-90 C in a hot-air, dehumidifying hopper dryer - to below about 0.05% moisture.

loserFacts.label: Failure mode
loserFacts.value: silver streaks (splay) on the visible surface

merges.loserName: Tool steel (P20 pre-hardened or H13/SKD61 hardened)
merges.survivorName: Tool steel: SKD61 / H13 / D2, the moulds and dies
merges.why: metal.die-steel is already named 'SKD61 / H13 / D2, the moulds and dies'. My sibling grade nodes c64.case.tooling.h13 and c64.case.tooling.p20 are not proposed for merge - they are grade detail the reviewer may want folded into the survivor's facts rather than kept
merges.loserDescription: Most 1980s housing tools were cut from pre-hardened P20-type steel (about HRC 30-35) so the tool could be finished-machined without distortion. Tools needing more polish cycles or more heat went to H13/SKD61, vacuum-hardened and tempered to HRC 44-50.

merges.why: chem.pvc.uses-c64 is the C64-specific PVC node; mine is a second, weaker copy
merges.loserDescription: The wire jackets, cable boots and some insulators in a C64 are PVC. PVC is made by polymerising vinyl chloride, and vinyl chloride comes from the chlor-ethylene route (EDC cracking to VCM plus HCl) or from oxychlorination of ethylene. The ethylene and the chlorine both come out of the same crackers and chlor-alkali plants that feed everything else.

merges.why: same polymer - duplicate-name warning
merges.loserDescription: Some C64 feet and small grommets are natural rubber, cis-1,4-polyisoprene, made by coagulating latex tapped from Hevea brasiliensis. Natural rubber has excellent resilience and grip and ages to a tacky amber.

loserFacts.label: Source
loserFacts.value: latex from Hevea brasiliensis plantations, coagulated with acetic acid

merges.why: same polymer - duplicate-name warning. Note c64.decor.screen-print.neoprene already takes its input from chem.rubber, not from my node
merges.loserDescription: Polychloroprene is used where oil and weather resistance matter - cable jackets on some Commodore leads, feet, and gasket material. It comes from chloroprene, made by chlorination of butadiene from the same C4 cracker cut.

merges.loserDescription: Bisphenol A polycarbonate appears in clear covers, lens and shroud parts and in some clear case variants. It is made from bisphenol A and phosgene, and from the same BPA that comes out of cumene/benzene oxidation.

merges.why: acetal homopolymer and copolymer; the survivor is the canonical POM node
merges.loserDescription: Acetal homopolymer and copolymer appear in precision mechanical parts - key plungers, small gears, latches - because POM is stiff, self-lubricating and dimensionally stable. It is made by polymerising formaldehyde from purified methanol.

loserFacts.label: Key property
loserFacts.value: low friction, high stiffness, good dimensional stability

merges.why: bisphenol A / epichlorohydrin epoxy; the survivor is the canonical node and already covers potting and die attach
merges.loserDescription: Epoxy resin is not a case material but appears as a potting and die-attach compound inside the machine - gluing the heat sink to the regulators and, in places, encapsulating a noisy analogue section. Epoxy comes from bisphenol A and epichlorohydrin, both aromatic-derived.

loserFacts.label: Cure
loserFacts.value: amine or anhydride, room temp to 120 C

merges.survivorName: General purpose polystyrene, bulk and suspension
merges.why: GPPS and HIPS; the survivor publishes both routes
merges.loserDescription: General-purpose and impact polystyrene appear in the C64's plastic inventory as packaging foam and tray material rather than in the case itself. Impact polystyrene is styrene polymerised in the presence of a polybutadiene graft rubber - the same architecture as ABS, one substitution away, with the acrylonitrile dropped. Both come from the same styrene feedstock as the case resin.

loserFacts.label: Where it appears
loserFacts.value: packaging foam and trays, not the case

merges.why: nylon 6,6 - duplicate-name warning. The survivor sits oddly deep (under a switch slider) for a general polymer; a rename or a move up would be an improvement, but that is the reviewer's call, not mine
merges.loserDescription: Nylon is the classic connector and latch material: tough, slightly elastic, and it takes a good insert or press-fit without cracking. It appears in the latch tabs and clips that hold connectors in the case.

loserFacts.label: Water absorption
loserFacts.value: ~8% for 6,6 - it changes dimension with humidity

merges.why: the carbon-loaded conductive pad is exactly the key dome chem.silicone.polymer.key-domes publishes
merges.loserDescription: The contact is a small pad of silicone rubber loaded with conductive carbon black. The carbon particles touch each other and carry a small current across the PCB pad when the pad is pressed down, closing the switch. It needs to be conductive enough to bridge the gold contact but resistive enough not to be a dead short.

loserFacts.label: Matrix
loserFacts.value: silicone rubber (VMQ), cured with a peroxide

merges.why: Same conductors. Note that the target is currently kind 'process' for a substance; see the retype entry below. 50-power's version has the strand figures (0.15-0.20 mm, about 30 strands for 1.0 mm2) which are worth keeping.
merges.loserDescription: Stranded rather than solid, because a cord is flexed at the strain relief and a solid conductor cracks there within a few years. Each strand is 0.15-0.20 mm bare copper wire; a 1.0 mm2 cord has roughly 30 strands.

merges.why: A sintered tantalum bead capacitor, described in both fragments. mb.passives.caps.tantalum is the richer node (13 nodes: anode pressing and sintering, the anodic Ta2O5 dielectric, the MnO2 solid electrolyte, packaging, the columbite ore-to-powder route and the early-1980s supply squeeze), so it should survive. The 0.22 uF 35 V epoxy-dipped bead used in the brick, and the note that a tantalum fails short, belong on c64.psu.aux-caps, where they already are.
merges.loserDescription: A porous sintered tantalum pellet, pressed from tantalum powder and sintered at 1200-2000 C under vacuum, dipped in manganese dioxide as the solid electrolyte, then coated with a conductive polymer or resin and epoxy for protection. Extremely high capacitance per unit volume and no liquid electrolyte to dry out, but it fails short and can burn.

loserFacts.label: Anode
loserFacts.value: sintered tantalum powder, ~99.9% Ta, grain size 1-3 um

loserFacts.label: Dielectric
loserFacts.value: manganese dioxide, grown electrochemically at 90-200 V

loserFacts.label: CV product
loserFacts.value: ~10,000 uF.V per cc - roughly 10x an aluminium electrolytic

loserFacts.label: Ore grade
loserFacts.value: Ta2O5 equivalent, typically 0.02-0.05% Ta2O5 in columbite

loserFacts.label: Refining
loserFacts.value: electron-beam melting / electron-beam floating zone to 99.9-99.99%

merges.why: Both name the 2N3055 / 2N3792 series-pass transistor of the brick's discrete regulator. 10-silicon's node is a bare leaf; 50-power's carries the triple-diffusion structure, the TO-3 package mass, the hermetic sealing and the emitter wire bonds, so it is the survivor under CHECKLIST 4.1. Re-point anything that references mb.discretes.power-bjt. Medium confidence on the 120407 discrete schematic either way - the note on the node says the part numbers are unconfirmed for this assembly.
merges.loserDescription: The 2N3055 is a 15 A, 200-300 V NPN power transistor in a TO-3 metal can or a plastic TO-220, used as the series pass element in the C64's linear 5 V power supply. The 2N3792 is a 100 V, 0.5 A NPN used in the supply's short-circuit detection, driving an SCR crowbar. Both are triple-diffused or epitaxial-base-collector designs with large dies, thick aluminium (or nickel) metallization and often a molybdenum or copper heat spreader, die-attachable with a soft solder or silver brazing.

loserFacts.label: 2N3055
loserFacts.value: NPN, 250 V VCEO, 15 A Ic, 200 W Pc

loserFacts.label: 2N3792
loserFacts.value: NPN, 100 V VCEO, 0.5 A Ic, 1 W Pc

merges.survivorName: The ABS grade the C64 case used
merges.why: The whole ABS subtree here re-derives what chem.abs.grade already states as the grade the C64 case used. merges.loserDescription: Acrylonitrile-butadiene-styrene: a SAN matrix rigidified by acrylonitrile, toughened by grafted polybutadiene and given surface gloss by styrene. Commodore bought commodity ABS pellets in 25 kg bags, compounded them with colour masterbatch in a merchant compounder, and shipped them to case factories in Hong Kong and Taiwan.

merges.loserDescription: A flexible cord with one heavier line conductor, one neutral and a green or green-and-yellow earth conductor, exiting the case through a clamp or grommet. The sheath is PVC in the 1980s rather than the older rubber; PVC is tougher, thinner and better suited to being moulded into the case.

loserFacts.label: Construction
loserFacts.value: stranded annealed copper in a PVC or rubber sheath

loserFacts.label: Rating
loserFacts.value: 2.5 A / 250 V for a light-duty appliance cord

loserFacts.label: Colour
loserFacts.value: black or white sheath; green or green/yellow earth in the North American build

merges.why: Same plug. I have already renamed mine to 'Moulded wall plug' so the two names no longer collide, which is a stopgap, not a fix: it is the NEMA 1-15P / CEE 7/16 end of the same cord. Merge with the cord above; the nickel-plated-brass contacts node travels with it.
merges.loserDescription: A two- or three-pole moulded plug permanently attached to the cord: in the North American build a polarised NEMA 1-15P with one blade rotated 180 degrees so it can only be inserted one way round; in most of Europe a CEE 7/16 Europlug with two round 4.0 mm pins. The body is a thermosetting or thermoplastic moulding with the cord entering through a separate bushing so the strain is not carried by the conductors.

merges.why: Both nodes are named 'Nickel reforming catalyst' and both are leaf materials at medium confidence. The 70-petrochem copy is the one on the canonical hydrogen-from-SMR path and is the richer of the two (it carries the pre-1957 Topsoe SMR-180 detail and the multi-bed reformer tube geometry). Kept per CHECKLIST keep-rule 1. This is the last of the duplicate-name groups left by the QA pass.
merges.loserDescription: Nickel oxide on alumina, or the classic nickel-molybdenum on alumina, formed by impregnating a porous pellet with nickel nitrate and calcining. Ends at the laterite and the bauxite.

merges.loserName: Scheelite and wolframite: the limestone vein alternative
merges.why: Phase 2. This node was always a tungsten ore node filed under molybdenum: its own name said 'the limestone vein alternative', i.e. relative to a molybdenum parent it was not really about. The previous pass recorded here that its description 'should be widened from molybdenum to both metals', which is the opposite of what it needed - it should have become a tungsten ore node. Its only real content was the greisen co-occurrence of scheelite CaWO4 and molybdenite MoS2, which is now a clause in metal.tungsten.ore and a clause in metal.molybdenum. The node also carried a build-process sentence about 'the point the brief made', which CHECKLIST 7a forbids.
merges.loserDescription: Almost all molybdenum came from porphyry copper, but there is a second source: the molybdenite that sits in the tungsten skarn and vein deposits - the Climax and Henderson molybdenum orebodies in Colorado were actually a Colorado Clueca-type porphyry with a molybdenum-bearing skarn. The relevant geology is that molybdenum and tungsten share the hydrothermal vein environment, and scheelite (CaWO4) and molybdenite (MoS2) are sometimes intergrown in the same greisen. So the molybdenum in a C64's injection-moulding die could in principle have come out of the same vein as a tungsten electrode - which is the point the brief made when it said no tungsten in a 1982 C64, and this is where that fact becomes interesting: the tungsten was there, in the same rock, but it went into other industries.

loserFacts.label: Molybdenite
loserFacts.value: MoS2 in vein and skarn greisen

loserFacts.label: Companion
loserFacts.value: scheelite CaWO4 and wolframite, often in the same vein

merges.why: Phase 2. Same name as the new canonical node, which is what the audit's duplicate-name rule flagged. The whole of the chemistry chain it described in one paragraph - digest to sodium tungstate, to APT, to WO3, hydrogen reduction, potassium doping, drawing - is now four real nodes under metal.tungsten, so a path-local copy that compressed four levels of supply chain into one description was the wrong shape as well as the wrong place. Its 'Korea and China were becoming dominant' note is now on metal.tungsten.ore.mine, where the supply claim belongs.
merges.loserDescription: Tungsten does not exist as a pure ore anywhere. Wolframite (Fe,Mn)WO4 and scheelite CaWO4 are decomposed with caustic soda or sodium carbonate to sodium tungstate, then to APT (ammonium paratungstate), then to tungsten trioxide reduced with hydrogen at 800-1000 degrees C to a fine powder, which is doped with potassium and drawn.

loserFacts.label: Reduction
loserFacts.value: 800-1000 degrees C, H2, to W powder

loserFacts.label: Drawing
loserFacts.value: doped powder, hydrogen-annealed, swaged and drawn to 0.04 mm

loserFacts.label: Purity
loserFacts.value: 99.9-99.95%, and the potassium content is controlled to control the grain

merges.why: Phase 2. Same name as the new canonical node. A mine is a facility, not a property of a television's heater, so the node belonged with the ore it produces. Its content is preserved verbatim in the survivor plus the 1980 supply shift.
merges.loserDescription: Wolframite is dense and refractory, so the ore is mined, crushed and gravity-concentrated or floated to a 60-70% WO3 concentrate. Because the ore is often a by-product of a tin or molybdenum mine, tungsten supply followed the fortunes of tin mining, and the price spiked hard whenever the tin market wobbled.

loserFacts.label: Mining
loserFacts.value: underground stoping and hand sorting, plus alluvial allutan placers on the Malay Archipelago tin belt

merges.survivorName: Bastnasite concentrate and the Mountain Pass carbonatite
merges.why: Phase 2. This is the duplicate half of the split TODO section 4 complains about: the europium phosphor and the samarium magnet each grew their own bastnasite story while this one grew a third. Bastnasite is an ore, so it belongs under metal.rare-earths next to monazite, not inside a rubber catalyst in a plastics fragment. Its note - 'the rare earth chain is a metals subsystem; this node marks where a 1980s rubber catalyst entered it' - was about the tree rather than the substance, which CHECKLIST 7a forbids; the metals link it complains about now exists for real.
merges.loserDescription: A light rare earth carbonate fluorosilicate, about 6-9% rare earth oxides, discovered in 1878 at Bastnas in Sweden and mined in quantity from 1949. It is the last dig-it-out node of the ABS branch's rubber phase: a C64's rubber comes from butadiene from a cracker, but the catalyst that gives that butadiene its cis content begins in a carbonatite dyke in California or in Inner Mongolia.

merges.survivorName: Bastnasite concentrate and the Mountain Pass carbonatite
merges.why: Phase 2. The fourth copy of the rare-earth ore story, and the vaguest: 'with the world supply dominated by one mining complex and its associated separation plants' names no complex, and its own note admits the chain is 'deliberately compressed'. The mineral it was pointing at now has a real node with the two named complexes and the separation step. Monazite, which this node's name also claimed, is now metal.rare-earths.monazite.
merges.loserDescription: Rare-earth minerals are worked chiefly from carbonatite and monazite/bastnaesite concentrates, with the world supply dominated by one mining complex and its associated separation plants. The oxides are then produced by acid leach and solvent extraction.

merges.loserName: Monazite, the thorium and rare-earth carrier
merges.survivorName: Monazite concentrate and the beach-sand placer
merges.why: Phase 2. Monazite was a duplicate mineral living under the tantalum branch, where it appears as an impurity to be filtered off a fluoride solution. That role is genuine and is kept - metal.tantalum.thorium still points here, and the survivor keeps the 5-30% ThO2 figure - but the mineral itself, its composition and its occurrence, belongs with the other rare-earth ore. Per CHECKLIST keep-rule 4 the name was relative to a parent ('the thorium and rare-earth carrier') and is now the general name.
merges.loserDescription: Monazite, (Ce,La,Nd,Th)PO4, is a heavy placer mineral from the same beach sands as the ilmenite and the rutile - the Kerala and Queensland and Cape Breton sands. It is the world's main thorium source and, after a very difficult separation, a rare-earth source. In the tantalum circuit monazite is an impurity that has to be filtered off the fluoride solution. So the tantalum in a 1982 capacitor, the titanium dioxide in its casing, and the thorium residue all come out of the same Queensland beach sand.

loserFacts.label: Occurrence
loserFacts.value: heavy placer concentrates from a beach sand

merges.loserName: Crude benzene from the coke oven
merges.why: same substance from the same route: crude benzol stripped from coke-oven gas. The wash-oil/steam-strip sentence has been folded into the survivor. Verdict 2026-10-03 (TODO carried-over item): not a co-product distinction, a duplicate.
merges.loserDescription: A 1982 coke oven produced a very large fraction of the world's synthetic benzene, and benzene was the root of the styrene-polystyrene, phenol-formaldehyde and epoxy industries - so this node is where the coal branch and the plastics branch join. The benzol was drawn out of the oven gas with a wash oil, and the wash oil was then steam-stripped. It is a dense, sweet-smelling, carcinogenic liquid and it is a document about the chemical industry that produced nylon, epoxy resin, phenol formaldehyde resin, styrene, and polyurethane precursors all at once.

loserFacts.label: Yield
loserFacts.value: 8-12 kg of benzene per tonne of coke

loserFacts.label: Route
loserFacts.value: wash oil absorption then steam stripping of the rich oil

loserFacts.label: In 1982
loserFacts.value: benzene was about 85-90% coal-based rather than petroleum-based; the coal route held on until roughly the 1990s-2000s before cracking economics killed it

merges.why: Vitreous enamel is the same lead-borosilicate glass family, applied as a slurry and baked as a coating rather than as a seal band. Only the material copy merges; the coating operation stays behind in the parent process node mb.passives.resistors.discrete-axial.wirewound.enamel, whose glass input re-points at the survivor. The survivor's batch route (silica, boric oxide, lead oxide, alkali) covers it.
merges.loserDescription: A glassy coating on the wound wire, applied as a slurry and baked. The enamel is what makes a wirewound part look like a glass-bodied component and is what lets it run hot without the wire oxidising.

merges.survivorName: Nylon 6,6 from adipic acid and HMDA
merges.why: Same polymer by the same route; second path-local copy with identical inputs (chem.polyamide.nylon-66, chem.petroleum). Fold the C64-use sentence (switch housings, joystick bushings, microswitch cases) and the chemistry note into the survivor before deleting. Move the ingredients row 'nylon' with it. Same pattern as the already-proposed peripheral.tv.crt.yoke.winding.bobbin.nylon merge into this survivor.
merges.loserDescription: The base polymer of the glass-filled nylon case, made from hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid. Caprolactam is the route to nylon 6, a different grade. A single C64 contains nylon in its switch housings, its joystick bushings and its microswitch cases.

merges.why: Same substance family: low-melting borosilicate fusing glass, batched from silica, boric oxide, lead oxide and alkali, applied as a paste and fired. The loser (a few per cent of glass wetting barium titanate grains to close porosity and seal the internal electrode) is the generic MLCC account; the survivor is the richer account (six facts: ~24 wt% PbO, 430-460 C seal, 600-700 C devitrification, 60-100 mesh print). Fold the BaTiO3-wetting and insulation-resistance sentences into the survivor before deleting.
merges.loserDescription: A few per cent of low-melting glass, added so that on sintering it wets the barium titanate grains, closes the porosity and gives the internal electrode a hermetic interface. Without it the MLCC is not gas-tight and its insulation resistance collapses.

merges.why: Same substance by the same route: boric acid from colemanite digested with sulphuric acid, calcium out as gypsum. The survivor carries the reaction, the sub-100 C drying limit and the 0.7-0.9 t yield with two sources at high confidence; the loser is a childless medium-confidence leaf. Union the loser's places (Boron/Kramer district, Bigadi Turkey) and its colemanite-diggings depth into the survivor. Kind friction is real and recorded: the survivor is typed process (it describes the digestion) while the loser is typed material (the acid); retype the survivor to material or keep the digestion as a child process. The parent funnel-glass batch already takes boric acid as an input, which resolves to the survivor through the ingredients table, so no edge dangles.
merges.loserDescription: Borates lower the glass's expansion coefficient and its melting point, which is exactly what a funnel that must survive a 25 kV implosion needs. Most borax for the western hemisphere came from borate ores in southern California and from Turkey.

merges.survivorName: Nylon 6,6 from adipic acid and HMDA
merges.why: Same polymer by the same route: nylon 6,6 from hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid, which the loser already takes as an input. The survivor is the published polymer node (salt formation, polymerisation conditions, butadiene-hydrocyanation feedstock route, Nylon 66 source). The loser is a path-local resin copy. Fold the loser's correction note (caprolactam makes nylon 6, not 6,6) into the survivor before deleting. This supersedes the 40-chassis proposal that made the loser the survivor for c64.case.other-polymers.nylon (a node no longer in the tree; that entry is stale): redirect it here too. Move the ingredients row 'nylon 6 6' with it.
merges.loserDescription: The base polymer of PA66, a condensation polymer of hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid - not of caprolactam, which makes nylon 6, a different nylon with a lower melting point. The 6,6 grade was preferred for mechanical parts because of its moisture stability and its higher melting point, and both of its monomers are petrochemical.

merges.why: Duplicates: the same conductive elastomer key domes at the same level (both kind part). The chem node is the path-local copy under the silicone branch (generic prose plus a C64 note); the 33-passives-c node is the machine-specific canonical dome (confidence high vs medium, 3 facts vs 2, sourced, with a made-of composition edge and a moulding chain). The 40-chassis dome nodes (conductive-rubber, silicone, carbon-black) are already merged away, so this completes the pair from the chemistry side. Re-pointings (1): chem.silicone.polymer children chem.silicone.polymer.key-domes -> c64.keyboard-switches.domes. Facts union: adopt Travel ~0.5-2 mm (survivor has none); force ranges overlap (loser 0.5-2 N is ~50-200 gf vs survivor 150-250 g dome-alone) so keep the survivor's and note the loser's. Flag: loser description says 8-12 mm travel, contradicting its own 0.5-2 mm fact and the 3-4 mm full-key travel; drop the 8-12 mm prose on apply.
merges.loserDescription: A switch contact made of a silicone or neoprene elastomer filled with carbon black - or with metal-plated hollow glass spheres - so that the rubber itself conducts. When the dome is pressed it shorts to a printed conductor beneath; the dome's force curve (about 0.5-2 N operating, 8-12 mm travel) is the feel of the keyboard. The conductive filler is a petroleum carbon black or a silvered microsphere, and the elastomer is usually a peroxide-cured silicone or a neoprene, chosen for its fatigue life in millions of actuations.

merges.why: Duplicates: the same two-piece ABS shell at the same level (both kind part). Description-first evidence: chem.abs.c64-case describes the moulded object (350-400 g per machine, beige/brown textured skin, vents moulded through the wall), not a resin grade; the grade already lives separately as chem.abs.grade (material), so no substance-vs-object split is lost. Re-pointings (1): chem.abs children chem.abs.c64-case -> c64.case. Facts union: adopt Approximate ABS mass ~0.35-0.4 kg and Moulding two-shot/multi-cavity with EDM texture (survivor has neither). Flag: loser says two-shot while survivor shows two separate mouldings (rear-shell + bezel); fold the two-shot wording as note, not fact.
merges.loserDescription: About 350-400 g of ABS: a two-shot moulding, the beige or brown textured skin over the structural frame, with the moulding texture itself - a fine leather grain applied by the tool's EDM process - as the only decoration. Behind the front bezel there is a metal RF shield and a plastic shield can, and the vents are moulded through the wall. Everything visible on the outside of a C64, apart from the keycaps and the badge, is this one polymer.

loserFacts.label: Moulding
loserFacts.value: two-shot / multi-cavity injection moulding with EDM texture

merges.why: Cassiterite (SnO2), the tin ore and smelter feed. Same substance at the same level: the chem copy ('Tin oxide, 78.8% tin by mass, the principal tin ore. The 78.8% is pure-mineral stoichiometry, not a distinct product grade, so this is NOT an ore-vs-concentrate level distinction. Keep-rule 2: metal.cassiterite is a shared published node in 60-metals; the chem copy is catalogue-only with zero in-tree references. Facts union: loser has no facts; its Llallagu/Cornwall/Kinta Valley places are already covered by the survivor's text (Bolivian shields, Cornwall, Malaysia/Indonesia); its dangling prose input 'cassiterite ore' resolves conceptually to the survivor itself via _ingredients 'tin ore' and dies with the loser. The loser's C64-scale solder-joint sentence belongs as a note on chem.solder-chemicals.solder-alloy (a 70-file edit, flagged for that owner, not moved here). No references to re-point (orphan; catalogue entry regenerates at build); no children to adopt.
merges.loserDescription: Tin oxide, 78.8% tin by mass, the principal tin ore. Recovered from placer deposits by panning and gravity concentration and from hard-rock veins by flotation, then smelted or reduced to tin. The C64-scale observation is the interesting one: a single soldered joint holds a few milligrams of tin, and there are a hundred and fifty million of them, so the tin industry exists in part because of solder joints.

API-grade barite at 4.28 g/cm3 added to a base mud of about 1.03-1.2... nearly insoluble in water') is the same dense graded barite as metal.barite.drilling-mud ('Drilling grade barite and its mud... gravity of at least 4.2... 90% passed 45 um... 100-300 tonnes of barite per kilometre'). merges.loserDescription: Columbite-tantalite is a solid solution of columbite and tantalite, mined both as placer gravels and as lode pegmatites. Concentrating it needs gravity, magnetic and electrostatic separation followed by an acid-leach circuit, because only a few per cent of the rock is Ta2O5; the concentrate may reach 10-30 % Ta2O5. Because the ore is bulk low-grade rock, mining and concentration - not the chemistry - is where most of the cost of a tantalum capacitor lives. Tantalum-bearing minerals are dense and so concentrate naturally in stream and beach placers below any pegmatite outcrop, and much of the 1980s supply was won by artisanal and semi-industrial alluvial mining in the Kivu highlands, which is exactly why ore supply could be disrupted by regional politics rather than by a mine closure. Historically the ore came from the Congo and from Rwanda-Burundi, which is precisely why Western capacitor supply chains were politically and economically exposed in this period.
